checks.claim: B1, free group: G_B<=C B, and explicitly G_B<=4B
checks.reason: Use the Bessel-unitary Fourier matrix from C3 Section7. The entry <xi>sin(v|xi|)/|xi| is at most sqrt2*max(1,|v|). The other entries are at most 1. The Frobenius bound gives at most sqrt(3+2B^2)<=sqrt5 B on E. The constant block tau(v) has norm (|v|+sqrt(v^2+4))/2<=B+1<=2B. The direct-sum norm is the maximum of the two, so G_B<=sqrt5 B<=4B for B>=1.

checks.claim: B1, primitive constant: C_B<=C B^(3-1/r) and C_B B^(1/r)>=B
checks.reason: Since B>=1, B^(1-1/r-theta)<=B^(1-1/r), so C_B<=2G_B^2 B^(1-1/r)<=32B^(3-1/r). For the lower bound, G_B>=||S_F(0)||=1, so C_B B^(1/r)>=G_B^2 B>=B.

checks.claim: B1, crude Young cost: log||S_F(ell)U_D(ell)||<=C_theta B(1+||D||_theta^nu) for 0<=ell<=B and D(0)=0, with C_theta depending only on theta
checks.reason: Follows from the piece counts in upper-young-perturbation Section2. Small d (c_theta d B^theta<=1/4): log sup||U_D||<=2c_theta B^theta d<=1/2. Large d: n_D<=2B(4c_theta d)^nu pieces, each of norm at most 4/3. Adding log||S_F(ell)||<=log(4B)<=C B gives the bound with a constant depending on theta only, not an arbitrary C(theta,B). The target correctly calls this a crude bound, not a factorization.

The primitive is linear in the field, and C3(13) without its sqrt(delta) factor (as in E2 Section4) applied to TPhi-barT_delta Phi on I_m gives e_m. For Hbar_m, C3(13) on the constant field barM_m gives C_B delta^(-1/r)|I_m|^(1/r)||barM_m||. Bochner-norm Jensen gives |I_m|^(1/r)||barM_m||<=||TPhi||_Lr(I_m), hence <=a_m. Empty cells give zero paths.

checks.claim: B2, good full blocks (a_m<=K): E1 multiplicative step with A=S_F(B), plus the S2 static bound at the exact lambda
checks.reason: Apply E1 with base path Hbar_m (||Hbar_m||_theta<=a_m<=K, starts at 0) and perturbation X=H_m-Hbar_m (x<=e_m, X(0)=0). This gives log||P_m^0||<=log||S_F(B)U_Hbar_m(B)||+C(theta,B,K)(e_m+e_m^nu). Here S_F(B)U_Hbar_m(B) is the actual physical constant-potential flow P_barM_m(B). This is the S2 Section5 identification, with interaction primitive D_V=int S_F(-s)L S_F(s)ds. barM_m lies in mathcalV_R by S4 (closed class, Bochner averages), and ||barM_m||<=K/B<=K, so S2 applies with this K. Result: log16+4log(1+K)+3log(1+B)+B lambda(barM_m). No eigenstate, gap, positive-potential assumption, or flow equality is used. The physical endpoint is kept.

checks.claim: B2, prefactor counting: the full-block count gives [log16+4log(1+K)+3log(1+B)]/B
checks.reason: The bracket is nonnegative, and the number of good full blocks is at most N. Since N=floor(1/(delta B)), delta N<=1/B. The last cell is never normalized as if it had length B.

checks.claim: B2, rate comparison: dropping bad, last and empty cells is the correct upper direction, and S4 makes the difference vanish uniformly
checks.reason: delta*B*lambda(barM_m)=int_{I_m} lambda(barT_delta Phi). Since lambda>=0 (S2: -K^2<=beta<=0), the sum over good blocks is at most int_I lambda(barT_delta Phi)<=Rate(Phi)+int_I|lambda(barT_delta Phi)-lambda(TPhi)|. The last term goes to 0 uniformly on the ball at fixed B by S4(5).

checks.claim: B2, Young error sum: delta*sum(e_m+e_m^nu)->0 uniformly, via the existing Mathlib power-mean type with exponents r and r/nu
checks.reason: Real.rpow_sum_le_const_mul_sum_rpow_of_nonneg with p=r>=1 on f=e_m>=0, and with p=r/nu>1 on f=e_m^nu>=0, card=n=N+1>=1. It gives delta*sum e<=(delta n)^(1-1/r)(delta*sum e^r)^(1/r) and delta*sum e^nu<=(delta n)^(1-nu/r)(delta*sum e^r)^(nu/r). With delta n<=2/B and the S4 Lr convergence, both go to 0 at fixed B, K, M before C(theta,B,K) matters. All rpow exponents are positive, so 0^x=0 is safe. No new kernel or count is needed.

checks.reason: a_m>K>=1 and nu<r give 1+a_m^nu<=(K^-r+K^(nu-r))a_m^r. Then delta*sum_bad C_theta B(1+a_m^nu)<=C_theta B C_B^r Z^r(K^-r+K^(nu-r))<=C_theta 32^r B^(3r) Z^r(...). So C=C_theta 32^r depends only on theta, r and the free-group convention, and Z=||T||M. No uniform maximum over blocks is used. The rate of bad blocks is dropped, which is valid because lambda>=0.

This is C_theta B delta[1+C_B^nu Z^nu delta^(-nu/r)]->0 because nu<r. The worst-case exponent delta^(1-nu/r) matches the 4 exact rows (n^-4 at delta=n^-9).

checks.claim: B3: M_B=M0 B^m, K_B=B^s with s>r(3+m)/(r-nu) makes both B2 terms and the log prefactor vanish
checks.reason: Log prefactor: [log16+4s*log(1+B)+3log(1+B)]/B->0 (using log(1+B^s)<=s*log(1+B)). Tails: C||T||^r M0^r B^(r(3+m))(B^(-sr)+B^(s(nu-r))). minor: falsification-v1.md lines 26-27 says the exact primitive gap -B^2 xi(1-xi)/2 is 'on the diagonal'. That holds only for the (1,1) entry; the (2,2) entry has the opposite sign, +B^2 xi(1-xi)/2. The script and JSON report only the (1,1) value. Name the entry.

target-v1 B1 uses a generic C. The explicit universal constants G_B<=4B (actually <=sqrt5 B) and C_B<=32B^(3-1/r) appear only in the crosswalk. Stating them in the target would make the B2 constant C=C_theta 32^r fully explicit.

target-v1 does not say that Hbar_m is the primitive stopped at ell_m and extended constantly on [0,B]. This does not matter, because the last positive cell is treated only with crude B1 and full cells have ell_m=B. Still, the definition should match C3 and E2.
The notation '||D||theta^nu' in B1 line 26 should read (||D||_theta)^nu, with ||.||_theta=sup+[.]_theta on [0,B] as in E1/E2.

The free-sector calibration (lines 80-85) is a lower bound on the B2 left side at Phi=0: the full rate there is log||S_F(B)||/B>=log||tau(B)||/B. It is consistent with the B2 prefactor because log||tau(B)||<=log(1+B). Saying explicitly that this is a consistency check on the prefactor would help.
Possible optional sharpening, not needed for B3: on good full blocks ||barM_m||<=K/B, so S2 could use max(1,K/B) instead of K.
